title: Ordering at a night market
setting: 士林夜市 on a Saturday night around nine. The lanes are packed shoulder to shoulder, the air smells of 臭豆腐 and grilled squid, and vendors shout over the crowd under bright bulbs.
ai_role: A friendly 阿姨 running a 蚵仔煎 stall who speaks quickly, calls everyone 帥哥 or 美女, mixes in Taiwanese words and uses lots of 喔 and 啦.
learner_role: A hungry visitor who wants to eat a few classic snacks and find out what else is good nearby.
goals: Order 蚵仔煎 with your sauce and spice preference
Say whether you will eat here or take it away and pay
Ask the 阿姨 to recommend another stall nearby

key_phrases.zh: 老闆，我要一份蚵仔煎，不要辣。
key_phrases.pinyin: lǎo bǎn, wǒ yào yí fèn é ā jiān, bú yào là
key_phrases.en: Boss, one oyster omelette please, not spicy.
key_phrases.note: 蚵仔煎 is usually said in Taiwanese: ô-á-tsian. In Mandarin people say é ā jiān or ô á jiān rather than the dictionary reading hé zǎi jiān.

key_phrases.pinyin: jiàng kě yǐ shǎo yì diǎn ma?
key_phrases.en: Could I have less sauce?
key_phrases.note: Taiwan says 一點, almost never 一點兒.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè ge zěn me mài?
key_phrases.en: How much is this?
key_phrases.note: Many Taiwanese pronounce 這個 as zhèi ge.

key_phrases.pinyin: nèi yòng hái shì wài dài?
key_phrases.en: For here or to go?
key_phrases.note: Taiwan terms. Mainland China says 堂食 and 打包.

key_phrases.zh: 我要外帶，可以幫我裝袋嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào wài dài, kě yǐ bāng wǒ zhuāng dài ma?
key_phrases.en: To go. Could you bag it for me?

key_phrases.zh: 可以用LINE Pay嗎？還是只收現金？
key_phrases.pinyin: kě yǐ yòng LINE Pay ma? hái shì zhǐ shōu xiàn jīn?
key_phrases.en: Can I use LINE Pay, or is it cash only?
key_phrases.note: Many stalls are still cash only, though LINE Pay and 街口支付 are spreading.

key_phrases.pinyin: fù jìn hái yǒu shén me hǎo chī de?
key_phrases.en: What else is good to eat around here?

native_tips: Vendors call any customer 帥哥 or 美女. Just accept it with a smile; denying it sounds odd.
There is no tipping and no bargaining over food prices.
Praise sounds natural as 好好吃喔 or 超好吃的, not 很好吃 said flatly.
Bins are scarce at night markets, so people carry their rubbish until they find one.
opening_line: 帥哥美女，來喔！蚵仔煎現煎的喔，很好吃啦！要幾份？

title: Parcel pickup and bill payment at 7-ELEVEN
setting: A 7-ELEVEN on a busy corner on a weekday evening. The door chime rings constantly, the hot food counter steams with 茶葉蛋 and 關東煮, and a line forms at the register.
ai_role: A young, efficient clerk who rattles off the standard questions (袋子、載具、集點) at high speed but is patient if you ask them to repeat.
learner_role: A customer who needs to collect an online order and pay a phone bill.
goals: Collect a store-to-store parcel by giving your name and the last three digits of your phone number
Pay a utility or phone bill with the barcode slip
Answer the clerk's questions about bags, e-receipt carrier and microwaving

key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ hǎo, wǒ yào qǔ huò.
key_phrases.en: Hi, I'm here to pick up a parcel.
key_phrases.note: 取貨 = collect a package (店到店 shipments from Shopee etc.).

key_phrases.zh: 我的手機末三碼是五八七。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ de shǒu jī mò sān mǎ shì wǔ bā qī.
key_phrases.en: The last three digits of my phone number are 587.
key_phrases.note: Clerks ask for your name and 末三碼 (also 後三碼).

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào jiǎo fèi, zhè shì zhàng dān.
key_phrases.en: I'd like to pay a bill. Here's the statement.

key_phrases.pinyin: bú yòng dài zi, xiè xie.
key_phrases.en: No bag, thanks.
key_phrases.note: Plastic bags cost NT$1-2, so the clerk will ask 要袋子嗎？

key_phrases.pinyin: fā piào bāng wǒ cún shǒu jī zài jù.
key_phrases.en: Please save the receipt to my phone carrier.
key_phrases.note: 載具 is a barcode in your phone that stores e-invoices (電子發票), which are also lottery tickets.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè ge kě yǐ bāng wǒ wéi bō ma?
key_phrases.en: Could you microwave this for me?
key_phrases.note: Taiwan reads 微 as wéi (ㄨㄟˊ); mainland standard is wēi.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè ge yǒu mǎi yī sòng yī ma?
key_phrases.en: Is this buy-one-get-one-free?

native_tips: People call 7-ELEVEN 小七 and FamilyMart 全家.
You will hear 歡迎光臨 on entry and 謝謝光臨 on leaving; no reply is needed.
Companies ask for 統編 (tax ID) on receipts; if you are not claiming expenses just say 不用.
Convenience stores also handle ticket printing, ibon kiosks, laundry and even traffic fines.
opening_line: 歡迎光臨！您好，請問要結帳嗎？

title: Ordering bubble tea
setting: A busy 手搖飲 shop next to an MRT exit at four in the afternoon. A wall-sized menu lists dozens of teas, and a queue of high-school students in uniform taps orders into their phones.
ai_role: A fast, cheerful clerk who expects orders in the standard format (item, size, sweetness, ice) and asks follow-ups if you forget one.
learner_role: A customer ordering drinks for yourself and a coworker.
goals: Order two drinks with size, sweetness (甜度) and ice level (冰塊)
Ask about toppings and extra cost
Handle the questions about bags and waiting for your number

key_phrases.zh: 我要一杯大杯珍珠奶茶，半糖少冰。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào yì bēi dà bēi zhēn zhū nǎi chá, bàn táng shǎo bīng.
key_phrases.en: One large pearl milk tea, half sugar, less ice.

key_phrases.pinyin: tián dù bīng kuài ne?
key_phrases.en: Sweetness and ice?
key_phrases.note: Sweetness: 正常糖/全糖, 少糖, 半糖, 微糖, 一分糖, 無糖. Ice: 正常冰, 少冰, 微冰, 去冰, 常溫, 溫, 熱.

key_phrases.pinyin: lǜ chá qù bīng wú táng.
key_phrases.en: Green tea, no ice, no sugar.

key_phrases.pinyin: kě yǐ gǎi chéng bō bà ma?
key_phrases.en: Can I switch to the big pearls?
key_phrases.note: 波霸 = large tapioca pearls; 珍珠 are often the smaller ones.

key_phrases.pinyin: jiā liào yào duō shǎo qián?
key_phrases.en: How much for a topping?

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè yàng jiù hǎo, bú yòng dài zi.
key_phrases.en: That's all, no bag needed.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhēn nǎi dà bēi bàn táng shǎo bīng.
key_phrases.en: Large pearl milk tea, half sugar, less ice (natural shorthand).
key_phrases.note: 珍奶 is the everyday short form of 珍珠奶茶.

native_tips: Give the order in one breath: item + size + sweetness + ice. Clerks will prompt you for anything missing.
Bringing your own cup (環保杯) usually gets a NT$5 discount.
Sweetness is also expressed as X分糖, e.g. 三分糖 = 30%.
If you just say 正常 for both, you will get very sweet tea with full ice.
opening_line: 嗨，你好！要喝什麼？甜度冰塊呢？

title: Breakfast at a 早餐店
setting: A 美而美-style breakfast shop at 7:20 on a weekday morning. The 阿姨 flips 蛋餅 on a hot iron griddle while the radio plays, and students and office workers grab bags of food on the way to the MRT.
ai_role: The 早餐店阿姨: warm, fast, remembers regulars' orders, calls everyone 帥哥 or 美女 and will happily chat about the weather.
learner_role: A regular customer grabbing breakfast before work or class.
goals: Order a 蛋餅 or 蘿蔔糕 and a drink with your preferences
Say whether you eat in or take away
Ask the total and handle sauce questions

key_phrases.zh: 阿姨，我要一個起司蛋餅，一杯大冰奶。
key_phrases.pinyin: ā yí, wǒ yào yí ge qǐ sī dàn bǐng, yì bēi dà bīng nǎi.
key_phrases.en: Auntie, a cheese egg crepe and a large iced milk tea.
key_phrases.note: 大冰奶 = large iced milk tea. 起司 is the Taiwan word for cheese (mainland 芝士/奶酪).

key_phrases.zh: 蘿蔔糕可以煎焦一點嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: luó bo gāo kě yǐ jiān jiāo yì diǎn ma?
key_phrases.en: Could you fry the turnip cake a bit crispier?

key_phrases.pinyin: tiě bǎn miàn yào hēi hú jiāo de.
key_phrases.en: Iron-plate noodles with black pepper sauce, please.
key_phrases.note: 鐵板麵 comes with 黑胡椒醬 or 蘑菇醬; a Taiwan breakfast classic.

key_phrases.pinyin: nèi yòng, wǒ zuò nà biān.
key_phrases.en: Eating here, I'll sit over there.

key_phrases.pinyin: tián là jiàng yì diǎn diǎn jiù hǎo.
key_phrases.en: Just a little sweet chili sauce.

key_phrases.pinyin: gēn zuó tiān yí yàng.
key_phrases.en: Same as yesterday.

key_phrases.pinyin: ā yí, zǒng gòng duō shǎo?
key_phrases.en: Auntie, how much altogether?

native_tips: 美而美 is a chain, but people use the name loosely for any Western-style breakfast shop.
Some shops let you tick your order on a paper slip (點餐單) and hand it in.
早餐店奶茶 is made from black tea and powder and tastes different from tea-shop milk tea; many Taiwanese are nostalgic about it.
Calling the owner 阿姨 or 老闆 is normal and friendly.
opening_line: 早安！帥哥（美女）要吃什麼？內用還是外帶？

title: Ordering 鹽酥雞
setting: A 鹽酥雞 stand on a street corner near a university at 11pm. Trays of raw skewers, vegetables and tofu sit under a lamp, with a stack of plastic baskets and tongs beside a bubbling fryer.
ai_role: The 老闆: a quiet young guy who takes your basket and asks the standard questions about spice, garlic, pepper and basil.
learner_role: A late-night snacker choosing items for a 宵夜.
goals: Pick items and hand over your basket
Specify spice level, garlic, pepper and basil
Ask how long it will take and pay

key_phrases.zh: 我要鹽酥雞、甜不辣跟四季豆。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào yán sū jī, tián bú là gēn sì jì dòu.
key_phrases.en: I'd like popcorn chicken, tempura fish cake and green beans.
key_phrases.note: 甜不辣 is a loan from Japanese tempura and means fried fish cake in Taiwan.

key_phrases.pinyin: xiǎo là jiù hǎo.
key_phrases.en: Just mildly spicy.

key_phrases.pinyin: suàn tóu yào, jiǔ céng tǎ yě yào.
key_phrases.en: Yes to garlic, and basil too.
key_phrases.note: 九層塔 = Thai basil, fried in at the end.

key_phrases.pinyin: hú jiāo fěn duō yì diǎn.
key_phrases.en: A bit more pepper powder.

key_phrases.pinyin: jī pái bú yào qiē.
key_phrases.en: Don't cut the chicken cutlet.
key_phrases.note: 雞排 can be ordered 切 or 不切.

key_phrases.pinyin: dà gài yào děng duō jiǔ?
key_phrases.en: About how long is the wait?

native_tips: The routine: take a basket, pick items with the tongs, hand the basket to the 老闆.
In the south it is often called 鹹酥雞; both names are fine.
Expect the questions 要辣嗎？要蒜嗎？胡椒？九層塔？ in rapid succession; 都要 means 'yes to everything'.
opening_line: 好，籃子給我。要辣嗎？蒜頭要不要？

title: MRT and EasyCard
setting: 台北車站 MRT concourse at 8:30 on a weekday. Commuters stream past the gates, the top-up machines have short queues, and a station attendant sits at the information counter.
ai_role: A patient MRT station attendant who explains lines, transfers and exits in clear, polite Mandarin.
learner_role: A newcomer who needs to top up an EasyCard and get to 台北101.
goals: Top up your 悠遊卡
Ask which line and transfer to take
Find the right platform direction and exit

key_phrases.zh: 請問悠遊卡在哪裡加值？
key_phrases.pinyin: qǐng wèn yōu yóu kǎ zài nǎ lǐ jiā zhí?
key_phrases.en: Excuse me, where can I top up my EasyCard?
key_phrases.note: 加值 = top up (mainland 充值).

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào jiā zhí wǔ bǎi kuài.
key_phrases.en: I'd like to add 500 dollars.

key_phrases.pinyin: qù tái běi yī líng yī yào zuò nǎ yì tiáo xiàn?
key_phrases.en: Which line goes to Taipei 101?
key_phrases.note: 101 is read yī líng yī in Taiwan; yāo for 1 is rare.

key_phrases.pinyin: yào zài nǎ yí zhàn zhuǎn chéng?
key_phrases.en: Where do I transfer?

key_phrases.zh: 往淡水的方向是這邊嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: wǎng dàn shuǐ de fāng xiàng shì zhè biān ma?
key_phrases.en: Is this the platform towards Tamsui?

key_phrases.pinyin: qǐng wèn jǐ hào chū kǒu bǐ jiào jìn?
key_phrases.en: Which exit number is closer?

native_tips: Say 捷運, not 地鐵.
No eating, drinking, or even chewing gum past the gates; fines are real.
Stand on the right on escalators in Taipei, and leave 博愛座 (priority seats) for those who need them; people are sensitive about this.
Tapping the card is 嗶卡 or 刷卡.
opening_line: 您好，請問需要什麼幫忙嗎？

title: Taking a taxi
setting: A rainy evening outside a department store in 信義區. Yellow cabs (小黃) crawl past in traffic, and you finally flag one down.
ai_role: A chatty middle-aged taxi driver (運將) who loves talking about food, traffic and the weather, speaking with a mild Taiwanese accent.
learner_role: A passenger going to 師大夜市.
goals: Give the destination politely
Ask about time and traffic, and give stopping directions
Pay by card or EasyCard and ask for a receipt

key_phrases.zh: 司機大哥，麻煩到師大夜市。
key_phrases.pinyin: sī jī dà gē, má fán dào shī dà yè shì.
key_phrases.en: Driver, to Shida Night Market please.
key_phrases.note: 麻煩 + destination is the natural polite form.

key_phrases.pinyin: dà gài yào duō jiǔ? huì sāi chē ma?
key_phrases.en: About how long? Will there be traffic?

key_phrases.pinyin: qián miàn lù kǒu tíng jiù hǎo.
key_phrases.en: Just stop at the next intersection.

key_phrases.pinyin: kě yǐ yòng yōu yóu kǎ ma?
key_phrases.en: Can I pay with EasyCard?
key_phrases.note: Many taxis accept EasyCard and credit cards; check the sticker.

key_phrases.zh: 不好意思，可以開慢一點嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: bù hǎo yì si, kě yǐ kāi màn yì diǎn ma?
key_phrases.en: Sorry, could you drive a bit slower?

key_phrases.pinyin: kě yǐ gěi wǒ shōu jù ma?
key_phrases.en: Could I have a receipt?

native_tips: 小黃 = taxi; 運將 (from Taiwanese ūn-tsiàng) = driver, used casually.
No tipping; round up only if you want to.
Drivers often start conversations; short friendly answers are fine.
Apps: Uber and 55688 (台灣大車隊) are common ways to call a cab.
opening_line: 你好，要去哪裡？

title: Getting a SIM card
setting: A telecom store near 台北車站 on a weekday afternoon. Posters advertise 吃到飽 data plans and the clerk has a stack of forms ready.
ai_role: A telecom shop clerk who speaks fast about 方案, 綁約 and 證件 but is happy to slow down.
learner_role: A newcomer who needs a Taiwanese number and mobile data.
goals: Ask for a prepaid card or a plan with unlimited data
Find out what ID is needed
Ask the price and whether there is a contract

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng bàn yì zhāng yù fù kǎ.
key_phrases.en: I'd like to get a prepaid SIM card.

key_phrases.zh: 有沒有上網吃到飽的方案？
key_phrases.pinyin: yǒu méi yǒu shàng wǎng chī dào bǎo de fāng àn?
key_phrases.en: Do you have an unlimited data plan?
key_phrases.note: 吃到飽 'all-you-can-eat' also means unlimited data.

key_phrases.pinyin: xū yào shén me zhèng jiàn?
key_phrases.en: What ID do I need?
key_phrases.note: Foreigners usually need a passport plus a second ID or ARC (居留證).

key_phrases.zh: 一個月多少錢？要綁約嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: yí ge yuè duō shǎo qián? yào bǎng yuē ma?
key_phrases.en: How much a month? Is there a contract?
key_phrases.note: 綁約 = lock-in contract.

key_phrases.pinyin: kě yǐ bāng wǒ shè dìng ma?
key_phrases.en: Could you set it up for me?

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ de shǒu jī hào mǎ shì duō shǎo?
key_phrases.en: What is my phone number?

native_tips: 門號 means a phone number/line; 辦門號 = sign up for a number.
The big three are 中華電信, 台灣大哥大 and 遠傳.
Taiwanese read phone numbers digit by digit, with 0 as líng.
opening_line: 您好，要辦門號還是預付卡？

title: Dinner at a 熱炒店 with friends
setting: A loud 一百元熱炒 restaurant on a Friday night, with plastic stools, round tables and fridges full of 台灣啤酒. Woks roar in the open kitchen and every table is toasting.
ai_role: 阿凱, your Taiwanese coworker: loud, generous, keeps proposing toasts and always orders too much food.
learner_role: A coworker out with friends after a long week.
goals: Choose and order several dishes to share
Order drinks and handle toasting etiquette
Decide how to split the bill

key_phrases.zh: 我們先點三杯雞、炒水蓮跟菜脯蛋。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men xiān diǎn sān bēi jī, chǎo shuǐ lián gēn cài fǔ dàn.
key_phrases.en: Let's start with three-cup chicken, stir-fried water lily stems and dried-radish omelette.
key_phrases.note: 菜脯 is often said in Taiwanese (tshài-póo).

key_phrases.pinyin: xiān lái sì píng tái pí.
key_phrases.en: Four bottles of Taiwan Beer to start.
key_phrases.note: 台啤 = Taiwan Beer; 18天 is the fresh 18-day version.

key_phrases.pinyin: gān bēi! — wǒ suí yì jiù hǎo.
key_phrases.en: Cheers! — I'll just sip.
key_phrases.note: 乾杯 literally means empty your glass; 隨意 lets you drink as much as you like.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè pán chāo xià fàn de.
key_phrases.en: This dish goes really well with rice.

key_phrases.pinyin: lǎo bǎn, zài lái yì wǎn bái fàn.
key_phrases.en: Boss, another bowl of rice.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men píng fēn ba.
key_phrases.en: Let's split it evenly.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè tān wǒ qǐng!
key_phrases.en: This round's on me!

native_tips: At many 熱炒店 you tick dishes on a paper menu yourself and hand it to staff.
Everything is shared; take from the plates with your own chopsticks unless serving chopsticks are provided.
People often settle up later with LINE Pay or bank transfer: 我再轉給你.
Say 隨意 when someone toasts you if you don't want to down your drink.
opening_line: 來來來，坐坐坐！今天辛苦了，你想吃什麼？三杯雞一定要的啦！

title: Booking Taiwan High Speed Rail
setting: The 高鐵台北站 ticket counter on a Friday afternoon before a long weekend. The departure board flickers, and families with luggage queue behind you.
ai_role: A polite, formal ticket clerk who uses 您 and 請問 and explains options clearly.
learner_role: A traveller heading to 高雄 (左營) for the weekend.
goals: Buy a ticket to 左營 for a specific time
Choose reserved seating and a window seat
Ask about discounts and changing the ticket

key_phrases.zh: 我要一張到左營的單程票。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào yì zhāng dào zuǒ yíng de dān chéng piào.
key_phrases.en: One single ticket to Zuoying, please.
key_phrases.note: 左營 is the Kaohsiung HSR station.

key_phrases.zh: 我要對號座，靠窗的位子。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào duì hào zuò, kào chuāng de wèi zi.
key_phrases.en: A reserved seat by the window, please.
key_phrases.note: 對號座 = reserved; 自由座 = non-reserved cars.

key_phrases.pinyin: yǒu méi yǒu zǎo niǎo yōu huì?
key_phrases.en: Are there early-bird discounts?

key_phrases.pinyin: xià yì bān jǐ diǎn kāi?
key_phrases.en: When does the next train leave?

key_phrases.pinyin: lái huí piào yǒu bǐ jiào pián yí ma?
key_phrases.en: Is a return ticket cheaper?
key_phrases.note: 有比較 + adjective is typical Taiwan Mandarin.

key_phrases.zh: 我想改票，改成明天早上的。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng gǎi piào, gǎi chéng míng tiān zǎo shàng de.
key_phrases.en: I'd like to change my ticket to tomorrow morning.

native_tips: Use 您 with staff; Taiwanese service language is quite formal.
The T Express app and convenience-store kiosks also sell tickets.
University students get a discount (大學生優惠) on some trains.
Choosing a seat is called 劃位.
opening_line: 您好，請問要到哪裡？幾點的車？

title: Taking a TRA train to 彰化
setting: 台北車站 TRA hall at noon. Announcements echo, and a kiosk sells the famous 台鐵便當 in paper boxes. You are heading to 彰化, the hometown setting of 《那些年，我們一起追的女孩》.
ai_role: First a TRA ticket clerk, then a 便當 vendor. Both are brisk but kind.
learner_role: A traveller going to 彰化 to see where the novel is set.
goals: Buy a 自強號 ticket for an afternoon train
Ask about seats and standing tickets
Buy a 台鐵便當 and find your platform

key_phrases.zh: 我要一張到彰化的自強號，下午一點左右的。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào yì zhāng dào zhāng huà de zì qiáng hào, xià wǔ yì diǎn zuǒ yòu de.
key_phrases.en: One 自強 express ticket to Changhua, around 1pm.

key_phrases.zh: 還有座位嗎？沒有的話站票也可以。
key_phrases.pinyin: hái yǒu zuò wèi ma? méi yǒu de huà zhàn piào yě kě yǐ.
key_phrases.en: Any seats left? If not, a standing ticket is fine.
key_phrases.note: 站票 = standing ticket (also 無座).

key_phrases.zh: 區間車可以刷悠遊卡嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: qū jiān chē kě yǐ shuā yōu yóu kǎ ma?
key_phrases.en: Can I use EasyCard on local trains?

key_phrases.zh: 我要一個台鐵便當，排骨的。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào yí ge tái tiě biàn dāng, pái gǔ de.
key_phrases.en: One TRA lunchbox, the pork chop one.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè bān chē huì tíng yuán lín ma?
key_phrases.en: Does this train stop at Yuanlin?

key_phrases.pinyin: qǐng wèn dì jǐ yuè tái?
key_phrases.en: Which platform?
key_phrases.note: 月台 = platform.

native_tips: Train types: 自強號 (express), 莒光號 (semi-express), 區間車 (local).
台鐵便當 with 排骨 is a nostalgic classic; eating it on the train is part of the experience.
In 2024 TRA became a state-owned company (臺灣鐵路公司), but everyone still says 台鐵.
opening_line: 您好，請問要到哪一站？幾點的車？

title: Renting a scooter
setting: A scooter rental shop next to 花蓮火車站 at nine in the morning. Rows of 125cc scooters stand outside, helmets hang on hooks, and the owner is hosing down the pavement.
ai_role: The shop owner: a laid-back 大哥 who checks your licence, explains the rules and warns you about 兩段式左轉.
learner_role: A tourist renting a scooter to ride to 太魯閣 and the coast.
goals: Rent a scooter for two days and show your licence
Ask about deposit, helmet and fuel
Ask about traffic rules such as two-stage left turns

key_phrases.zh: 我想租一台機車，租兩天。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng zū yì tái jī chē, zū liǎng tiān.
key_phrases.en: I'd like to rent a scooter for two days.
key_phrases.note: 機車 = scooter/motorbike in Taiwan (mainland 摩托車). 很機車 is also slang for 'annoying'.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yǒu guó jì jià zhào.
key_phrases.en: I have an international driving permit.

key_phrases.pinyin: yā jīn yào duō shǎo?
key_phrases.en: How much is the deposit?

key_phrases.pinyin: ān quán mào yǒu fù ma?
key_phrases.en: Does it come with a helmet?

key_phrases.pinyin: jiǔ wǔ wú qiān, jiā mǎn.
key_phrases.en: 95 unleaded, fill it up.
key_phrases.note: Gas station attendants usually pump for you and ask 加多少？

key_phrases.zh: 這個路口要兩段式左轉嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: zhè ge lù kǒu yào liǎng duàn shì zuǒ zhuǎn ma?
key_phrases.en: Do I need to do a two-stage left turn here?
key_phrases.note: Scooters often must wait in the 待轉區 box to turn left.

native_tips: 機車 (vehicle) vs 很機車 (annoying) is a classic pun.
Many rental shops refuse riders without a valid Taiwan or international licence.
Electric sharing scooters (WeMo, GoShare) are common in cities.
opening_line: 你好，要租車喔？駕照帶了嗎？

title: Seeing a doctor at a clinic
setting: A neighbourhood 耳鼻喉科 clinic at 6:30pm. The waiting room is full, a screen shows the current number, and a nurse calls names from the counter.
ai_role: First the front-desk nurse (掛號), then a brisk but kind doctor. The AI plays both roles.
learner_role: A patient with a sore throat and cough.
goals: Register with your 健保卡
Describe your symptoms and how long you've had them
Ask how to take the medicine and request a doctor's note

key_phrases.zh: 你好，我要掛號，這是我的健保卡。
key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ hǎo, wǒ yào guà hào, zhè shì wǒ de jiàn bǎo kǎ.
key_phrases.en: Hi, I'd like to register. Here's my NHI card.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ shì chū zhěn.
key_phrases.en: It's my first visit.
key_phrases.note: 初診 = first visit; 複診 = follow-up.

key_phrases.zh: 我喉嚨痛，還有一點發燒。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ hóu lóng tòng, hái yǒu yì diǎn fā shāo.
key_phrases.en: I have a sore throat and a slight fever.

key_phrases.pinyin: yǐ jīng ké sou sān tiān le.
key_phrases.en: I've been coughing for three days.
key_phrases.note: Taiwan dictionary reading of 咳嗽 is ㄎㄜˊ ˙ㄙㄡ.

key_phrases.zh: 這個藥要飯前吃還是飯後吃？
key_phrases.pinyin: zhè ge yào yào fàn qián chī hái shì fàn hòu chī?
key_phrases.en: Should I take this before or after meals?

key_phrases.zh: 可以開診斷證明嗎？我需要請假。
key_phrases.pinyin: kě yǐ kāi zhěn duàn zhèng míng ma? wǒ xū yào qǐng jià.
key_phrases.en: Could you write a medical certificate? I need to take sick leave.

key_phrases.pinyin: guà hào fèi duō shǎo?
key_phrases.en: How much is the registration fee?
key_phrases.note: You pay 掛號費 plus a small 部分負擔 (copay).

native_tips: Taiwanese usually go to an 耳鼻喉科 (ENT) clinic for colds.
Clinics often dispense medicine on site in labelled 藥包 for three days.
Doctors are addressed as 醫生 (or 醫師 more formally).
opening_line: 您好，有帶健保卡嗎？是初診還是複診？

title: At the pharmacy
setting: A community pharmacy at 9pm, shelves of vitamins and cold remedies, with a pharmacist in a white coat behind the counter.
ai_role: A knowledgeable, careful pharmacist (藥師) who asks about allergies and explains dosage.
learner_role: A customer with a runny nose who also needs to pick up a prescription.
goals: Ask for cold medicine and describe symptoms
Mention an allergy and ask about side effects
Ask about dosage and fill a prescription

key_phrases.zh: 請問有沒有感冒藥？我有點流鼻水。
key_phrases.pinyin: qǐng wèn yǒu méi yǒu gǎn mào yào? wǒ yǒu diǎn liú bí shuǐ.
key_phrases.en: Do you have cold medicine? I have a bit of a runny nose.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè ge chī le huì xiǎng shuì jiào ma?
key_phrases.en: Will this make me sleepy?

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ duì pán ní xī lín guò mǐn.
key_phrases.en: I'm allergic to penicillin.
key_phrases.note: Penicillin is 盤尼西林 (or 青黴素).

key_phrases.pinyin: yì tiān chī jǐ cì? yí cì jǐ kē?
key_phrases.en: How many times a day, and how many pills each time?
key_phrases.note: Taiwan uses 顆 for pills.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào ná chǔ fāng jiān de yào.
key_phrases.en: I'm here to pick up a prescription.
key_phrases.note: 處方箋 = prescription slip.

key_phrases.pinyin: yǒu méi yǒu hóu táng?
key_phrases.en: Do you have throat lozenges?

native_tips: Many people ask for medicine by brand, e.g. 普拿疼 (Panadol).
Chronic patients use a 連續處方箋 to refill at pharmacies.
Pharmacists commonly double-check 有沒有過敏？ before selling.
opening_line: 你好，哪裡不舒服？

title: A LINE call with a classmate
setting: Sunday night, 10pm. You get a LINE voice call from a classmate about the group report due on Tuesday; you can hear a TV in the background on her side.
ai_role: 小美, a cheerful but stressed classmate who uses lots of 欸, 齁, 對啊 and 真的假的.
learner_role: A student in the same group project.
goals: Check on each other's progress on the report
Divide the remaining work
End the call naturally

key_phrases.zh: 欸，你現在方便講電話嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: ê, nǐ xiàn zài fāng biàn jiǎng diàn huà ma?
key_phrases.en: Hey, is now a good time to talk?
key_phrases.note: 欸 sounds like 'eh'. Taiwan says 講電話 for talking on the phone.

key_phrases.zh: 報告的簡報你做到哪了？
key_phrases.pinyin: bào gào de jiǎn bào nǐ zuò dào nǎ le?
key_phrases.en: How far have you got with the slides for the report?
key_phrases.note: 簡報 = slides/presentation (Taiwan).

key_phrases.zh: 我剛剛傳給你了，你看一下。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ gāng gāng chuán gěi nǐ le, nǐ kàn yí xià.
key_phrases.en: I just sent it to you, take a look.
key_phrases.note: 傳 = send a message or file.

key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ zěn me yǐ dú bù huí la!
key_phrases.en: Why did you read my message and not reply!
key_phrases.note: 已讀不回 'read, no reply' is a famous LINE complaint.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men fēn gōng yí xià hǎo le.
key_phrases.en: Let's divide up the work.

key_phrases.pinyin: nà jiù xiān zhè yàng, bāi bāi.
key_phrases.en: OK, that's it for now, bye.
key_phrases.note: 先這樣 is the standard way to wrap up a call.

native_tips: 打LINE給你 means to call someone on LINE.
Calls usually end with a chain: 好～那先這樣～掰掰～掰～.
Stickers (貼圖) are used as replies in chats; a sticker alone can mean OK.
opening_line: 喂～欸你在幹嘛？你有看到老師在群組說的嗎？

title: A night at KTV
setting: A private KTV room at 錢櫃 at 1am during the cheap late-night slot. A fruit platter and fries sit on the table, lights flash and the next song is already queued.
ai_role: 阿哲, a friend who hogs the microphone, loves 五月天 and pushes everyone to sing.
learner_role: A friend who is a bit shy to sing in Chinese.
goals: Choose and queue a song
Ask to move a song up, skip one or change the key
Agree to a duet and ask how long the room is booked

key_phrases.zh: 幫我點一首五月天的〈突然好想你〉。
key_phrases.pinyin: bāng wǒ diǎn yì shǒu wǔ yuè tiān de tú rán hǎo xiǎng nǐ.
key_phrases.en: Queue Mayday's 'Suddenly Miss You' for me.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè shǒu kě yǐ chā gē ma?
key_phrases.en: Can we bump this song to the front?
key_phrases.note: 插歌 = move a song up the queue.

key_phrases.pinyin: qiē diào qiē diào, zhè shǒu tài nán le!
key_phrases.en: Skip it, skip it, this one is too hard!

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men yì qǐ hé chàng ba!
key_phrases.en: Let's sing it together!

key_phrases.pinyin: yīn tài gāo le, kě yǐ jiàng Key ma?
key_phrases.en: It's too high, can we lower the key?

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men bāo xiāng kāi dào jǐ diǎn?
key_phrases.en: Until what time is our room booked?

native_tips: The big chains are 錢櫃 and 好樂迪; late-night 歡唱 packages are cheapest.
Classic crowd-pleasers: 五月天, 周杰倫, 蔡依林, and 台語歌 like 〈愛拼才會贏〉 for older crowds.
Cheering lines: 好聽！再來一首！安可！
opening_line: 換你啦！你要唱什麼？不唱不行喔！

title: Waiting for a typhoon day off
setting: The evening before a typhoon makes landfall. Wind rattles the windows of your apartment, and you and your roommate keep refreshing the news for the 停班停課 announcement.
ai_role: 阿翔, your roommate, who is overexcited about a possible 颱風假 and keeps reading comments on the mayor's Facebook page.
learner_role: A roommate who has work tomorrow.
goals: Find out whether work and school are cancelled
Plan supplies for the storm
Talk about safety and complain about the weather

key_phrases.zh: 明天到底有沒有放颱風假？
key_phrases.pinyin: míng tiān dào dǐ yǒu méi yǒu fàng tái fēng jià?
key_phrases.en: So is there a typhoon day off tomorrow or not?

key_phrases.zh: 台北市宣布停班停課了！
key_phrases.pinyin: tái běi shì xuān bù tíng bān tíng kè le!
key_phrases.en: Taipei has announced work and school are off!

key_phrases.zh: 我們要不要先去全聯買泡麵跟水？
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men yào bú yào xiān qù quán lián mǎi pào miàn gēn shuǐ?
key_phrases.en: Should we go to PX Mart for instant noodles and water first?

key_phrases.pinyin: chuāng hù yào tiē jiāo dài ma?
key_phrases.en: Should we tape the windows?

key_phrases.zh: 風雨好大，最好不要出門。
key_phrases.pinyin: fēng yǔ hǎo dà, zuì hǎo bú yào chū mén.
key_phrases.en: The wind and rain are really strong, better not go out.

key_phrases.zh: 結果外面根本沒什麼風雨嘛！
key_phrases.pinyin: jié guǒ wài miàn gēn běn méi shén me fēng yǔ ma!
key_phrases.en: Turns out there's hardly any wind or rain at all!
key_phrases.note: Grumbling about a 'wasted' typhoon day (or not getting one) is a Taiwanese tradition.

native_tips: Each city or county government decides 停班停課, usually announced in the evening.
People stock up on instant noodles, and vegetables become expensive after typhoons.
颱 and 台 are different characters: 颱風 is always written with 颱.
opening_line: 欸！颱風好像轉向了，你覺得明天會放假嗎？我一直在刷新聞！

title: Catching the garbage truck
setting: 7:30pm on a weekday. The melody of 〈少女的祈禱〉 drifts down the street as the garbage truck approaches, and neighbours hurry out holding bags of rubbish and recycling.
ai_role: 陳太太, your next-door neighbour: helpful, a bit bossy, and very serious about sorting rubbish.
learner_role: A newcomer in the building who has never taken out the rubbish in Taiwan.
goals: Find out when and where the truck comes
Learn how to sort general waste, recycling and food scraps
Ask what to do if you miss the truck

key_phrases.pinyin: lè sè chē jǐ diǎn huì lái?
key_phrases.en: What time does the garbage truck come?
key_phrases.note: Taiwan's dictionary reading of 垃圾 is lè sè (ㄌㄜˋ ㄙㄜˋ); lā jī is also widely heard.

key_phrases.zh: 這首音樂是〈少女的祈禱〉嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: zhè shǒu yīn yuè shì shào nǚ de qí dǎo ma?
key_phrases.en: Is this music 'A Maiden's Prayer'?
key_phrases.note: Trucks play 〈少女的祈禱〉 or 〈給愛麗絲〉 (Für Elise).

key_phrases.pinyin: bǎo tè píng yào diū nǎ lǐ?
key_phrases.en: Where do PET bottles go?
key_phrases.note: 寶特瓶 = plastic PET bottle.

key_phrases.zh: 廚餘要分生的跟熟的嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: chú yú yào fēn shēng de gēn shóu de ma?
key_phrases.en: Do food scraps need to be split into raw and cooked?
key_phrases.note: Rules vary by city. 熟 is often read shóu in Taiwan.

key_phrases.zh: 一般垃圾一定要用專用垃圾袋嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: yì bān lè sè yí dìng yào yòng zhuān yòng lè sè dài ma?
key_phrases.en: Does general rubbish have to go in the official bags?
key_phrases.note: Taipei and New Taipei charge through official pay-per-bag bags.

key_phrases.zh: 我錯過垃圾車了，怎麼辦？
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ cuò guò lè sè chē le, zěn me bàn?
key_phrases.en: I missed the truck, what do I do?

native_tips: Rubbish is handed directly to the truck; there are almost no public bins.
A recycling truck (資源回收車) follows the garbage truck.
In Taipei there is no collection on Wednesdays and Sundays.
追垃圾車 'chasing the garbage truck' is a shared Taiwanese experience.
opening_line: 欸，你是新搬來的喔？垃圾車快來了，你的垃圾有分類好嗎？

title: At the post office
setting: A 中華郵政 branch at lunchtime. Two queues: one for postal services (郵務) and one for savings (儲匯). You take a number and wait with a box under your arm.
ai_role: A brisk, helpful postal clerk.
learner_role: A customer sending a parcel to a friend in 台南 and another to family abroad.
goals: Send a parcel within Taiwan and ask the price
Compare air and sea mail for an overseas package
Declare the contents and buy a box

key_phrases.zh: 我要寄一個包裹到台南。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào jì yí ge bāo guǒ dào tái nán.
key_phrases.en: I'd like to send a parcel to Tainan.

key_phrases.pinyin: jì guà hào yào duō shǎo qián?
key_phrases.en: How much for registered mail?
key_phrases.note: 掛號 means registered mail here, and 'register' at a clinic.

key_phrases.pinyin: dà gài jǐ tiān huì dào?
key_phrases.en: About how many days will it take?

key_phrases.zh: 寄到美國，航空跟海運差多少？
key_phrases.pinyin: jì dào měi guó, háng kōng gēn hǎi yùn chà duō shǎo?
key_phrases.en: To the US, what's the difference between air and sea mail?

key_phrases.zh: 裡面是衣服跟書，沒有易碎品。
key_phrases.pinyin: lǐ miàn shì yī fú gēn shū, méi yǒu yì suì pǐn.
key_phrases.en: It's clothes and books inside, nothing fragile.
key_phrases.note: Many Taiwanese say 衣服 with a full second tone: yī fú.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào mǎi yí ge zhǐ xiāng.
key_phrases.en: I'd like to buy a box.

native_tips: The post office is also a bank; many people have a 郵局帳戶.
Take a 號碼牌 for the right counter type.
平信 = ordinary mail, 限時 = express, 掛號 = registered.
opening_line: 您好，寄東西嗎？寄到哪裡？

title: Getting a haircut
setting: A neighbourhood hair salon on a Saturday afternoon. Pop music plays, and an assistant gives you the famous Taiwan-style seated shampoo with a long scalp massage before the cut.
ai_role: Kevin, a chatty stylist (設計師) who asks about your job and keeps suggesting a perm or a colour.
learner_role: A customer who wants a trim and maybe a new colour.
goals: Describe the cut you want and the length
Comment on the shampoo massage and ask for adjustments
Discuss colour or styling and decline upselling politely

key_phrases.zh: 我想剪短一點，大概剪掉三公分。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng jiǎn duǎn yì diǎn, dà gài jiǎn diào sān gōng fēn.
key_phrases.en: I'd like it a bit shorter, about 3 cm off.

key_phrases.pinyin: liú hǎi bú yào tài duǎn.
key_phrases.en: Don't make the fringe too short.

key_phrases.pinyin: kě yǐ bāng wǒ dǎ báo ma?
key_phrases.en: Could you thin it out?

key_phrases.zh: 洗頭的力道可以再大一點。
key_phrases.pinyin: xǐ tóu de lì dào kě yǐ zài dà yì diǎn.
key_phrases.en: The shampoo massage could be a bit firmer.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ de tóu fǎ hěn róng yì luàn.
key_phrases.en: My hair gets messy easily.
key_phrases.note: Taiwan reads 髮 as fǎ (ㄈㄚˇ); mainland fà.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng rǎn shēn kā fēi sè.
key_phrases.en: I'd like to dye it dark brown.

key_phrases.pinyin: bāng wǒ zhuā yí xià jiù hǎo.
key_phrases.en: Just style it a bit with wax.
key_phrases.note: 抓 = style hair with wax or clay.

native_tips: Stylists are called 設計師, and the shampoo is often done by an assistant.
Seated shampoo with massage (洗頭) is a Taiwan speciality; some people go just for that.
To decline extras politely: 今天先剪就好，下次再說。
opening_line: 嗨，先幫你洗頭喔！水溫可以嗎？今天想怎麼剪？

title: Joining a gym
setting: A 24-hour chain gym in 板橋 on a weekday evening. Treadmills face a wall of screens, and a trainer with a tablet greets you at the front desk.
ai_role: Andy, an enthusiastic personal trainer (教練) who explains memberships and very much wants to sell you a package of 一對一 sessions.
learner_role: Someone thinking of joining the gym and doing a trial session.
goals: Ask about membership plans and contracts
Explain your training goals
Talk through a short workout and negotiate PT sessions

key_phrases.zh: 我想了解一下會員方案。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng liǎo jiě yí xià huì yuán fāng àn.
key_phrases.en: I'd like to learn about the membership plans.

key_phrases.pinyin: yào bǎng yuē ma? yuè jiǎo duō shǎo?
key_phrases.en: Is there a contract? How much per month?

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng liàn hé xīn gēn tuǐ.
key_phrases.en: I want to train core and legs.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè ge zhòng liàng huì bú huì tài zhòng?
key_phrases.en: Is this weight too heavy?

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xiū xí yí xià, chuǎn yí xià.
key_phrases.en: Let me rest and catch my breath.

key_phrases.zh: 一對一教練課一堂多少錢？
key_phrases.pinyin: yī duì yī jiào liàn kè yì táng duō shǎo qián?
key_phrases.en: How much is one personal training session?

native_tips: 重訓 = weight training, 有氧 = cardio.
Trainers commonly push package deals; 我考慮看看 is a polite way to stall.
Encouragement you will hear: 加油！再一下！最後兩下！
opening_line: 嗨！第一次來嗎？今天想練哪裡？

title: Grocery run at 全聯 and Costco
setting: Sunday afternoon. First a quick stop at the neighbourhood 全聯福利中心, then a drive to the huge Costco (好市多) in 中和, where the car park is full and sample stands draw crowds.
ai_role: 小琪, your roommate: a bargain hunter who knows every 全聯 promotion and wants to split Costco's giant packs.
learner_role: A roommate doing the weekly shopping.
goals: Compare deals and use a member card
Agree how to split bulk items
Handle checkout and paying each other back

key_phrases.zh: 全聯今天衛生紙有特價喔！
key_phrases.pinyin: quán lián jīn tiān wèi shēng zhǐ yǒu tè jià o!
key_phrases.en: Toilet paper is on sale at PX Mart today!

key_phrases.zh: 你有全聯福利卡嗎？可以集點。
key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ yǒu quán lián fú lì kǎ ma? kě yǐ jí diǎn.
key_phrases.en: Do you have a PX Mart card? You can collect points.

key_phrases.zh: 好市多的東西都好大包，我們分一分吧。
key_phrases.pinyin: hǎo shì duō de dōng xī dōu hǎo dà bāo, wǒ men fēn yì fēn ba.
key_phrases.en: Everything at Costco comes in huge packs, let's split it.
key_phrases.note: Many Taiwanese say 東西 with a full first tone on 西.

key_phrases.zh: 這邊有試吃，要不要吃吃看？
key_phrases.pinyin: zhè biān yǒu shì chī, yào bú yào chī chī kàn?
key_phrases.en: There's a free sample here, want to try?

key_phrases.pinyin: kǎo jī mǎi yì zhī huí qù hǎo le.
key_phrases.en: Let's grab a roast chicken.
key_phrases.note: 隻 is the measure word for animals (and roast chickens).

key_phrases.zh: 你先付，我等一下轉給你。
key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ xiān fù, wǒ děng yí xià zhuǎn gěi nǐ.
key_phrases.en: You pay first, I'll transfer you my share later.

native_tips: Costco is called 好市多 in Taiwan; 全聯 is the everyday budget supermarket.
Friends often 揪團 to share Costco bulk packs.
Bags are not free; bring your own or buy one at checkout.
opening_line: 走走走，去好市多！今天週末人一定爆多，我們要速戰速決喔。

title: Hiking 象山 at sunset
setting: 象山步道 at 5pm on a clear autumn day. Steep stone steps climb through the trees, mosquitoes buzz, and a crowd waits at 六巨石 for the sunset behind 台北101.
ai_role: 小芸, an energetic hiking friend who has done this trail twenty times and is merciless about rest breaks.
learner_role: A friend who is less fit and very sweaty.
goals: Complain about the climb and negotiate a rest
Ask how far is left to the viewpoint
Take photos and react to the view

key_phrases.zh: 樓梯也太多了吧，我腿好痠。
key_phrases.pinyin: lóu tī yě tài duō le ba, wǒ tuǐ hǎo suān.
key_phrases.en: That's way too many stairs, my legs are sore.

key_phrases.zh: 還要走多久才到觀景台？
key_phrases.pinyin: hái yào zǒu duō jiǔ cái dào guān jǐng tái?
key_phrases.en: How much further to the viewing platform?

key_phrases.zh: 我們在這邊休息一下好不好？
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men zài zhè biān xiū xí yí xià hǎo bù hǎo?
key_phrases.en: Can we rest here for a bit?

key_phrases.pinyin: bāng wǒ gēn yī líng yī pāi yì zhāng!
key_phrases.en: Take a photo of me with 101!

key_phrases.pinyin: xì yáng hǎo měi o, zhí dé le.
key_phrases.en: The sunset is gorgeous, it was worth it.
key_phrases.note: Taiwan reads 夕 as xì (ㄒㄧˋ); mainland xī.

key_phrases.zh: 有帶防蚊液嗎？蚊子好多。
key_phrases.pinyin: yǒu dài fáng wén yì ma? wén zi hǎo duō.
key_phrases.en: Did you bring mosquito repellent? So many mosquitoes.
key_phrases.note: Taiwan reads 液 as yì (ㄧˋ); mainland yè.

native_tips: Taiwanese often say 爬山 even for short city hikes.
Common encouragement: 快到了！再撐一下！
Bring water and repellent; 小黑蚊 bites are notorious in some areas.
opening_line: 加油！再爬一下就到了，今天天氣這麼好，夕陽一定超美！

title: A pickup basketball game
setting: An outdoor court at a junior high school at 5pm. The sun is low, a few groups are shooting around, and one team is a player short.
ai_role: 小胖, a competitive high-schooler who trash-talks playfully and argues about every foul.
learner_role: Someone who wants to join a game.
goals: Ask to join and agree on the rules
Communicate during play (passing, fouls, scoring)
Finish the game and arrange to play again

key_phrases.pinyin: kě yǐ jiā wǒ yí ge ma?
key_phrases.en: Can I join?

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men lái dòu niú, sān duì sān.
key_phrases.en: Let's play a three-on-three half-court game.
key_phrases.note: 鬥牛 = half-court pickup game.

key_phrases.pinyin: xiān gōng shí yī fēn de yíng.
key_phrases.en: First to eleven wins.

key_phrases.pinyin: chuán gěi wǒ, wǒ yǒu kòng dàng!
key_phrases.en: Pass it, I'm open!
key_phrases.note: Taiwan reads 檔 as dàng (ㄉㄤˋ).

key_phrases.pinyin: gāng gāng nà ge shì fàn guī ba!
key_phrases.en: That was a foul just now!

key_phrases.pinyin: hǎo qiú!
key_phrases.en: Nice shot!

key_phrases.pinyin: dǎ de bú cuò o, xià cì zài yuē.
key_phrases.en: Good game, let's play again sometime.

native_tips: Basketball is huge in Taiwanese schools; the novel's boys play constantly.
Trash talk is light and friendly: 你很弱欸！/ 防不住啦！
約打球 = arrange to play; 揪人 = round people up.
opening_line: 欸，你要打嗎？我們剛好缺一個，來鬥牛啊！

title: Viewing an apartment
setting: A fourth-floor walk-up in 公館 on a Sunday afternoon. You found the 套房 on 591; the landlady meets you at the iron gate with a ring of keys.
ai_role: 房東 王太太: practical, slightly guarded, talks fast about house rules, and wants a reliable long-term tenant.
learner_role: A young professional looking for a studio near the MRT.
goals: Ask about rent, deposit and what fees are included
Ask how electricity is charged and about house rules
Negotiate lease length and subsidies

key_phrases.zh: 這間套房一個月租金多少？
key_phrases.pinyin: zhè jiān tào fáng yí ge yuè zū jīn duō shǎo?
key_phrases.en: How much is the rent for this studio per month?
key_phrases.note: 套房 = room with private bathroom; 雅房 = room with shared bathroom.

key_phrases.pinyin: yā jīn yào jǐ ge yuè?
key_phrases.en: How many months' deposit?
key_phrases.note: Two months is typical.

key_phrases.zh: 管理費跟水電費有包含嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: guǎn lǐ fèi gēn shuǐ diàn fèi yǒu bāo hán ma?
key_phrases.en: Are the management fee and utilities included?

key_phrases.pinyin: diàn fèi yí dù zěn me suàn?
key_phrases.en: How is electricity charged per unit?
key_phrases.note: 度 = kWh. Landlords often charge a fixed rate per 度 via a sub-meter.

key_phrases.pinyin: kě yǐ shēn qǐng zū wū bǔ tiē ma?
key_phrases.en: Can I apply for the rent subsidy?
key_phrases.note: Some landlords refuse because it means declaring rental income.

key_phrases.pinyin: kě yǐ yǎng chǒng wù ma?
key_phrases.en: Are pets allowed?

key_phrases.pinyin: zuì duǎn yào zū duō jiǔ?
key_phrases.en: What's the minimum lease?

key_phrases.pinyin: yǒu duì wài chuāng ma?
key_phrases.en: Is there a window facing outside?
key_phrases.note: Many cheap rooms only have windows onto an airshaft or corridor.

native_tips: 591 is the main rental website; listings use 套房, 雅房, 整層 and 頂樓加蓋 (rooftop addition, cheap but hot).
Ask 房東 about 修繕 (repairs): who pays if the water heater breaks?
Landladies often address you as 你 and expect you to say 王太太 or 王姐.
opening_line: 你好，你是來看房子的喔？進來吧，鞋子脫在外面就好。

title: Office small talk at lunch
setting: A Taipei office at 12:10. Colleagues are ordering lunchboxes, someone is organising a group buy of desserts, and the lights will go off at 12:30 for the afternoon nap.
ai_role: 佳穎, a friendly colleague who organises every 團購 and knows all the office gossip.
learner_role: A coworker who joined the company a few months ago.
goals: Join the lunch order and a group buy
Chat about the weekend and overtime
Mention upcoming leave

key_phrases.pinyin: jīn tiān zhōng wǔ yào dìng biàn dāng ma?
key_phrases.en: Are we ordering lunchboxes today?

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yào yí ge jī tuǐ biàn dāng.
key_phrases.en: A chicken leg lunchbox for me.

key_phrases.zh: 你要不要跟團購？這家甜點超好吃。
key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ yào bú yào gēn tuán gòu? zhè jiā tián diǎn chāo hǎo chī.
key_phrases.en: Want to join the group buy? This dessert place is amazing.
key_phrases.note: 跟團 or +1 means you're in.

key_phrases.zh: 昨天又加班到十點，好累喔。
key_phrases.pinyin: zuó tiān yòu jiā bān dào shí diǎn, hǎo lèi o.
key_phrases.en: Worked overtime till ten again yesterday, so tired.

key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ zhōu mò yǒu qù nǎ lǐ wán ma?
key_phrases.en: Did you go anywhere at the weekend?
key_phrases.note: 有 + verb for past events is typical Taiwan Mandarin.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xià lǐ bài yào qǐng tè xiū.
key_phrases.en: I'm taking annual leave next week.
key_phrases.note: 特休 = paid annual leave; 禮拜 is common for 'week'.

native_tips: Many offices switch off the lights for 午休 (12:30-13:30) and people nap at their desks.
揪 = to rally people: 揪團, 揪吃飯, 有人要揪嗎？
Greeting colleagues leaving: 辛苦了！ / 先走囉！
opening_line: 欸，你中午要吃什麼？我們要揪團訂便當喔！

title: The company 尾牙 banquet
setting: A hotel banquet hall in January. Round tables of ten, a stage with a lucky-draw screen, departments performing dances, and the boss walking from table to table toasting.
ai_role: 林協理, a jovial, slightly tipsy senior manager seated next to you, who keeps toasting and teasing about the lucky draw.
learner_role: An employee at your first 尾牙.
goals: Toast your manager with an appropriate phrase
Chat about the lucky draw and prizes
Talk about your department's performance and drink politely

key_phrases.zh: 協理，我敬您一杯，謝謝您這一年的照顧。
key_phrases.pinyin: xié lǐ, wǒ jìng nín yì bēi, xiè xie nín zhè yì nián de zhào gù.
key_phrases.en: Director, a toast to you, thank you for looking after me this year.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhù gōng sī míng nián yè jì cháng hóng!
key_phrases.en: Here's to the company's success next year!

key_phrases.pinyin: jīn nián de tóu jiǎng shì shén me?
key_phrases.en: What's the grand prize this year?

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ zhǐ chōu dào cān jiā jiǎng ér yǐ.
key_phrases.en: I only got the participation prize.

key_phrases.zh: 我們部門要表演跳舞，好丟臉喔。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men bù mén yào biǎo yǎn tiào wǔ, hǎo diū liǎn o.
key_phrases.en: Our department has to perform a dance, so embarrassing.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ bú tài huì hē, wǒ suí yì.
key_phrases.en: I can't drink much, I'll just sip.

native_tips: 尾牙 comes from the last 做牙 (offering to 土地公) of the lunar year, on the 16th of the 12th month; companies hold banquets around then.
Bosses often 加碼 (add extra cash prizes) on the spot.
Toast seniors with both hands on the glass and your glass slightly lower than theirs.
opening_line: 來來來，今年辛苦啦！等一下抽獎，你覺得自己會不會中頭獎？

title: A first date
setting: Saturday afternoon at 華山1914文創園區, then a quiet café nearby. You were introduced by a mutual friend and have been chatting on LINE for two weeks.
ai_role: 小安, a slightly shy but witty person who opens up once the conversation gets going.
learner_role: Someone on a first date who wants to see the other person again.
goals: Greet and apologise for being late
Ask about interests and share your own
Suggest a second date and end the evening warmly

key_phrases.zh: 等很久了嗎？不好意思，我捷運坐過站了。
key_phrases.pinyin: děng hěn jiǔ le ma? bù hǎo yì si, wǒ jié yùn zuò guò zhàn le.
key_phrases.en: Have you been waiting long? Sorry, I missed my MRT stop.

key_phrases.zh: 你平常放假都在做什麼？
key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ píng cháng fàng jià dōu zài zuò shén me?
key_phrases.en: What do you usually do on your days off?

key_phrases.zh: 我覺得跟你聊天很開心。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ jué de gēn nǐ liáo tiān hěn kāi xīn.
key_phrases.en: I really enjoy talking with you.

key_phrases.zh: 下次要不要一起去看電影？
key_phrases.pinyin: xià cì yào bú yào yì qǐ qù kàn diàn yǐng?
key_phrases.en: Want to see a movie together next time?

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè cì wǒ qǐng, xià cì huàn nǐ.
key_phrases.en: My treat this time, yours next time.

key_phrases.pinyin: dào jiā gēn wǒ shuō yì shēng o.
key_phrases.en: Let me know when you get home, OK?
key_phrases.note: A very common caring line after a date.

native_tips: 曖昧 is the 'something going on but not official' stage; dating officially starts after 告白.
Splitting the bill is common now, but offering to treat with 下次換你 keeps things going.
Avoid being too direct at first; humour and 欸/啦 soften things.
opening_line: 嗨！你到了喔？我也剛到。要不要先找個地方坐？

title: Chatting with 阿嬤 at Lunar New Year
setting: 除夕 (New Year's Eve) at 阿嬤's house in 鹿港, 彰化. The family gathers around the hotpot for 圍爐, the TV new-year special is on, and kids are already counting red envelopes.
ai_role: 阿嬤, about 80, who speaks Mandarin with a strong Taiwanese accent and slips into Taiwanese (呷飽未、乖孫、歹勢). She is loving, keeps feeding you and asks when you'll get married.
learner_role: A grandchild (or a grandchild's partner) visiting for the holiday.
goals: Give New Year greetings and thank 阿嬤 for the 紅包
Talk about the food and traditions at the table
Deflect questions about marriage and jobs politely

key_phrases.zh: 阿嬤，新年快樂！祝您身體健康、長命百歲！
key_phrases.pinyin: ā mā, xīn nián kuài lè! zhù nín shēn tǐ jiàn kāng, cháng mìng bǎi suì!
key_phrases.en: Grandma, happy New Year! Wishing you good health and a long life!
key_phrases.note: 阿嬤 is a-má in Taiwanese; in Mandarin people say ā mā or ā mà.

key_phrases.pinyin: ā mā, nín chī bǎo le méi?
key_phrases.en: Grandma, have you eaten?
key_phrases.note: In Taiwanese: 呷飽未？(tsia̍h-pá--buē?), a standard greeting.

key_phrases.pinyin: dǎi shì dǎi shì, wǒ lái wǎn le.
key_phrases.en: Sorry, sorry, I'm late.
key_phrases.note: 歹勢 from Taiwanese pháinn-sè, 'sorry/embarrassed'.

key_phrases.pinyin: xiè xie ā mā de hóng bāo!
key_phrases.en: Thank you for the red envelope, Grandma!

key_phrases.zh: 長年菜要整根吃，才會長壽。
key_phrases.pinyin: cháng nián cài yào zhěng gēn chī, cái huì cháng shòu.
key_phrases.en: You eat the longevity greens whole so you'll live long.

key_phrases.zh: 我還沒有對象啦，不要急啦。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ hái méi yǒu duì xiàng la, bú yào jí la.
key_phrases.en: I'm not seeing anyone yet, don't rush me.

key_phrases.pinyin: ā mā, wǒ bāng nín jiā cài.
key_phrases.en: Grandma, let me serve you some food.

native_tips: Elders show love through food; saying 我吃很飽了 several times is normal.
Learn a few Taiwanese words: 呷飽未, 乖孫, 歹勢, 好食 (hó-tsia̍h).
Nosy questions (結婚了沒？薪水多少？) are expected at 過年; deflect with humour.
Never say 4 (四 sounds like 死) or talk about death during the holiday.
opening_line: 乖孫，你回來啦！呷飽未？來來來，阿嬤煮了你最愛吃的！

title: Praying at a temple
setting: 龍山寺 in 萬華 on a weekday morning. Incense smoke curls up to the carved roof, worshippers lay out fruit and cookies as offerings, and the clack of 擲筊 blocks echoes on the stone floor.
ai_role: A kind temple volunteer (志工阿伯) who explains every ritual step by step and slips into Taiwanese.
learner_role: A first-time visitor who wants to pray properly and ask 月老 about love.
goals: Learn the order of worship and how to hold the incense
Draw a fortune stick and cast moon blocks
Ask about 月老 and where to give an offering

key_phrases.zh: 請問拜拜的順序是什麼？
key_phrases.pinyin: qǐng wèn bài bai de shùn xù shì shén me?
key_phrases.en: What is the order for praying here?
key_phrases.note: 拜拜 (bài bai) = to worship; 掰掰 (bāi bāi) = bye-bye.

key_phrases.zh: 要先跟神明說自己的名字跟地址嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: yào xiān gēn shén míng shuō zì jǐ de míng zi gēn dì zhǐ ma?
key_phrases.en: Should I first tell the gods my name and address?
key_phrases.note: Taiwan reads 址 as zhǐ (ㄓˇ).

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng qiú qiān, yào zěn me zuò?
key_phrases.en: I'd like to draw a fortune, how do I do it?

key_phrases.zh: 擲筊擲到聖筊才算數嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: zhí jiǎo zhí dào shèng jiǎo cái suàn shù ma?
key_phrases.en: Does it only count if I get a 'yes' throw?
key_phrases.note: 聖筊 (one flat, one round side up) = yes; 笑筊 (both flat up) = the gods laugh, ask again; 陰筊 (both round up) = no.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng gēn yuè lǎo qiú yīn yuán.
key_phrases.en: I'd like to ask the Old Man under the Moon for a good match.

key_phrases.pinyin: xiāng yóu qián yào fàng zài nǎ lǐ?
key_phrases.en: Where do I put the offering money?

native_tips: Pray to each deity in the order the temple posts; tell them your name, birthday and address before your wish.
Many temples have reduced incense use; follow the signs.
A 籤詩 (fortune poem) can be explained at the 解籤 desk.
opening_line: 少年仔，第一次來喔？香先拿好，阿伯跟你講怎麼拜。

title: Opening a bank account
setting: A bank branch at 9:30am. You take a number from the machine, the waiting area is quiet, and a teller calls you to window 5.
ai_role: A meticulous bank teller (行員) who explains forms and documents carefully and formally.
learner_role: A newcomer (or someone starting a new job) who needs a local account for salary.
goals: Open an account and present the right ID
Ask about a debit card and online banking
Ask about fees and passbook updates

key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ hǎo, wǒ xiǎng kāi yí ge zhàng hù.
key_phrases.en: Hello, I'd like to open an account.

key_phrases.pinyin: xū yào dài nǎ xiē zhèng jiàn?
key_phrases.en: Which documents do I need?
key_phrases.note: Taiwanese bring 身分證 plus a 第二證件; foreigners bring an ARC (居留證) and passport.

key_phrases.zh: 我沒有印章，可以用簽名嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ méi yǒu yìn zhāng, kě yǐ yòng qiān míng ma?
key_phrases.en: I don't have a seal, can I sign instead?
key_phrases.note: Many banks still use a 印章 (personal seal) with the passbook.

key_phrases.zh: 我想申請金融卡跟網路銀行。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng shēn qǐng jīn róng kǎ gēn wǎng lù yín háng.
key_phrases.en: I'd like a debit card and online banking.

key_phrases.pinyin: kuà háng zhuǎn zhàng yào shǒu xù fèi ma?
key_phrases.en: Are there fees for transfers to other banks?

key_phrases.pinyin: cún zhé yào zài nǎ lǐ bǔ dēng?
key_phrases.en: Where do I update my passbook?
key_phrases.note: 補登 = print recent transactions in the passbook.

native_tips: Banks call this 辦理開戶; staff use very formal Mandarin (請問您今天要辦理什麼業務？).
Salary accounts (薪轉戶) often come with free transfers.
The passbook (存摺) is still widely used alongside apps.
opening_line: 您好，請問今天要辦理什麼業務？

title: Returning a faulty item
setting: An electronics store in a shopping district on a weekday evening. You bought wireless earphones last week and the left earbud stopped working.
ai_role: A polite store clerk who sticks to policy and needs the 發票 and original packaging.
learner_role: A customer who wants a refund or exchange.
goals: Explain the problem clearly
Show proof of purchase and request a return
Negotiate an exchange or refund method

key_phrases.zh: 你好，我上禮拜買的耳機有問題，想退貨。
key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ hǎo, wǒ shàng lǐ bài mǎi de ěr jī yǒu wèn tí, xiǎng tuì huò.
key_phrases.en: Hi, the earphones I bought last week are faulty, I'd like to return them.

key_phrases.pinyin: zuǒ ěr wán quán méi yǒu shēng yīn.
key_phrases.en: The left side has no sound at all.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yǒu dài fā piào gēn hé zi.
key_phrases.en: I brought the receipt and the box.
key_phrases.note: 發票 = official receipt (also a lottery ticket).

key_phrases.zh: 如果不能退，可以換一個新的嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: rú guǒ bù néng tuì, kě yǐ huàn yí ge xīn de ma?
key_phrases.en: If I can't return it, can I exchange it for a new one?

key_phrases.pinyin: tuì kuǎn huì tuì dào xìn yòng kǎ ma?
key_phrases.en: Will the refund go back to my credit card?

key_phrases.zh: 網購不是有七天鑑賞期嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: wǎng gòu bú shì yǒu qī tiān jiàn shǎng qí ma?
key_phrases.en: Don't online purchases have a 7-day return period?
key_phrases.note: 鑑賞期 is the legal 7-day cooling-off period for online orders. Taiwan reads 期 as qí.

native_tips: Keep the 發票; stores rarely process returns without it.
退貨 = return for refund, 換貨 = exchange.
Stay polite; Taiwanese service staff respond well to 麻煩你 and 不好意思.
opening_line: 您好，請問有什麼需要幫忙的嗎？

title: Complaining about a food delivery
setting: A rainy weeknight. Your foodpanda order arrived fifty minutes late, the soup spilled all over the bag, and one drink is missing. You open the in-app chat with customer service.
ai_role: A scripted but polite customer service agent (客服) who needs order details and photos before offering compensation.
learner_role: A hungry, annoyed customer.
goals: Describe exactly what went wrong
Provide evidence and ask for compensation
Stay fair to the delivery rider while complaining

key_phrases.zh: 我的訂單少了一杯飲料。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ de dìng dān shǎo le yì bēi yǐn liào.
key_phrases.en: My order is missing a drink.

key_phrases.zh: 湯整個灑出來了，袋子都濕了。
key_phrases.pinyin: tāng zhěng ge sǎ chū lái le, dài zi dōu shī le.
key_phrases.en: The soup spilled everywhere and the bag is soaked.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ děng le kuài yí ge xiǎo shí.
key_phrases.en: I waited almost an hour.

key_phrases.zh: 我可以上傳照片給你們。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ kě yǐ shàng chuán zhào piàn gěi nǐ men.
key_phrases.en: I can upload photos for you.

key_phrases.zh: 可以退款還是給折價券？
key_phrases.pinyin: kě yǐ tuì kuǎn hái shì gěi zhé jià quàn?
key_phrases.en: Can you refund me or give a discount voucher?
key_phrases.note: Taiwan reads 券 as quàn.

key_phrases.zh: 外送員也很辛苦，我不是要怪他。
key_phrases.pinyin: wài sòng yuán yě hěn xīn kǔ, wǒ bú shì yào guài tā.
key_phrases.en: The rider works hard too, I'm not blaming him.

native_tips: Taiwan says 外送 (not 外賣) and 外送員 or 外送師 for riders.
Customer service phrasing is very formal: 造成您的不便，深感抱歉。
Many people leave a 評價 (rating) afterwards; 給一星 = give one star.
opening_line: 您好，這裡是客服中心，很抱歉造成您的不便，請問訂單發生了什麼問題呢？

title: A beach trip to 墾丁
setting: 墾丁 in July. The sun blazes over 南灣, scooters line the beach road, and at night 墾丁大街 fills with food stalls and bars.
ai_role: 阿德, the owner of your 民宿 (B&B) in 恆春: laid-back, sunburnt, full of tips and warnings about the sun and currents.
learner_role: A tourist on a three-day trip with friends.
goals: Ask for activity recommendations (snorkelling, sights)
Ask about safety and weather
Arrange transport and check what the B&B includes

key_phrases.zh: 我們想去浮潛，哪裡比較推薦？
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men xiǎng qù fú qián, nǎ lǐ bǐ jiào tuī jiàn?
key_phrases.en: We want to go snorkelling, where do you recommend?

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè biān de làng huì bú huì tài dà?
key_phrases.en: Are the waves too big here?

key_phrases.zh: 防曬一定要擦，太陽超毒。
key_phrases.pinyin: fáng shài yí dìng yào cā, tài yáng chāo dú.
key_phrases.en: You have to wear sunscreen, the sun is brutal.
key_phrases.note: 太陽很毒 = the sun is harsh.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǎn shàng kěn dīng dà jiē hǎo guàng ma?
key_phrases.en: Is Kenting Street fun to walk around at night?

key_phrases.zh: 可以幫我們叫車去鵝鑾鼻燈塔嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: kě yǐ bāng wǒ men jiào chē qù é luán bí dēng tǎ ma?
key_phrases.en: Could you call us a car to Eluanbi Lighthouse?

key_phrases.pinyin: mín sù yǒu fù zǎo cān ma?
key_phrases.en: Does the B&B include breakfast?

native_tips: 民宿 owners are a great source of local tips and often arrange tours.
Southern Taiwanese speech is more Taiwanese-influenced and relaxed; expect 齁 and 啦 a lot.
恆春 is also famous from the film 《海角七號》.
opening_line: 歡迎來墾丁！外面很熱齁？先喝杯冰的。你們明天想去哪裡玩？

title: A hot spring in 北投
setting: 北投 on a cold, drizzly January evening. Steam rises from 地熱谷, the streets smell faintly of sulphur, and your hotel offers both a public bath and private rooms.
ai_role: A polite front-desk attendant at a hot spring hotel who explains prices and etiquette.
learner_role: A visitor who has never been to a Taiwanese hot spring.
goals: Compare public baths and private rooms
Ask about prices, time limits and swimwear rules
Learn bathing etiquette and safety

key_phrases.zh: 請問大眾池跟湯屋差在哪裡？
key_phrases.pinyin: qǐng wèn dà zhòng chí gēn tāng wū chà zài nǎ lǐ?
key_phrases.en: What's the difference between the public bath and a private room?
key_phrases.note: 大眾池 = shared bath (often nude, single-sex); 湯屋 = private room rented by the hour.

key_phrases.pinyin: tāng wū yí ge xiǎo shí duō shǎo qián?
key_phrases.en: How much is a private room per hour?

key_phrases.pinyin: dà zhòng chí yào chuān yǒng yī ma?
key_phrases.en: Do I need a swimsuit for the public bath?

key_phrases.pinyin: pào zhī qián yào xiān chōng zǎo ma?
key_phrases.en: Do I need to shower before soaking?
key_phrases.note: 沖澡 = rinse/shower; note 沖, not 衝.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè shì shén me quán zhí?
key_phrases.en: What kind of spring water is this?
key_phrases.note: Taiwan reads 質 as zhí (ㄓˊ). 北投 has 白磺泉 and 青磺泉.

key_phrases.zh: 泡太久會頭暈，要多喝水。
key_phrases.pinyin: pào tài jiǔ huì tóu yūn, yào duō hē shuǐ.
key_phrases.en: Soaking too long makes you dizzy, drink plenty of water.

native_tips: 泡湯 = to soak in a hot spring.
Rinse first, keep your towel out of the water and tie up long hair.
Rules on swimwear differ: hotel 大眾池 are usually nude, outdoor public pools require swimwear.
opening_line: 歡迎光臨！今天好冷齁，最適合泡湯了。請問要泡大眾池還是湯屋？

title: Studying for the 學測 with a classmate
setting: A 24-hour K書中心 in December, two weeks before the 學測 (university entrance exam). Desks are piled with 參考書 and past papers, and everyone whispers.
ai_role: 品妤, a diligent classmate who quizzes you, worries about her scores and secretly wants to get into 台大.
learner_role: A high-school senior preparing for the exam.
goals: Compare progress on past papers
Ask for and give help on a question
Talk about university choices and take a break

key_phrases.zh: 你數學考古題寫到第幾年了？
key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ shù xué kǎo gǔ tí xiě dào dì jǐ nián le?
key_phrases.en: Which year of the maths past papers are you up to?

key_phrases.zh: 這題我完全看不懂，可以教我嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: zhè tí wǒ wán quán kàn bù dǒng, kě yǐ jiāo wǒ ma?
key_phrases.en: I don't understand this question at all, can you teach me?

key_phrases.zh: 我模擬考考得好爛，好崩潰喔。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ mó nǐ kǎo kǎo de hǎo làn, hǎo bēng kuì o.
key_phrases.en: I did terribly in the mock exam, I'm falling apart.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men lái hù xiāng kǎo dān zì ba.
key_phrases.en: Let's quiz each other on vocab.

key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ xiǎng tián nǎ ge kē xì?
key_phrases.en: Which department are you going to put down?
key_phrases.note: 填志願 = list your university/department choices.

key_phrases.pinyin: K shū K dào tóu hǎo tòng.
key_phrases.en: I've studied so hard my head hurts.
key_phrases.note: K書 = cram/study hard, said with the letter K.

native_tips: The novel is set in the 1990s, when students sat the 大學聯考 (聯考); today it's the 學測 and 分科測驗.
崩潰 and 爆炸 are everyday exaggerations for stress.
Students call cram schools 補習班 and the exam-prep years 高三.
opening_line: 欸，你來了喔！我剛剛做了一回模擬考，社會好難，等一下我們對一下答案好不好？

title: Talking to a cram school teacher
setting: A cram school on 南陽街 at 9pm on a Tuesday. Fluorescent lights hum, students eat lunchboxes in the corridor before the next class, and score rankings are posted on the wall.
ai_role: 張老師, a sharp, encouraging cram-school homeroom teacher (班導) who also wants you to sign up for extra classes.
learner_role: A high-school student struggling with physics.
goals: Discuss your recent test results
Ask about joining a class and the fees
Talk about stress and make a study plan

key_phrases.zh: 老師，物理的課可以插班嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: lǎo shī, wù lǐ de kè kě yǐ chā bān ma?
key_phrases.en: Teacher, can I join the physics class midway?

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè qí de xué fèi shì duō shǎo?
key_phrases.en: How much is the fee for this term?
key_phrases.note: Taiwan reads 期 as qí.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ shàng cì xiǎo kǎo kǎo de hěn làn.
key_phrases.en: I did badly in the last quiz.

key_phrases.pinyin: lù yǐng kè kě yǐ bǔ kàn ma?
key_phrases.en: Can I watch the recorded class to make up?

key_phrases.zh: 我壓力好大，覺得自己念不完。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ yā lì hǎo dà, jué de zì jǐ niàn bù wán.
key_phrases.en: I'm so stressed, I feel I can't get through it all.
key_phrases.note: Taiwan uses 念書 for studying.

key_phrases.zh: 謝謝老師，我會再努力的。
key_phrases.pinyin: xiè xie lǎo shī, wǒ huì zài nǔ lì de.
key_phrases.en: Thank you, I'll keep working hard.

native_tips: 南陽街 near 台北車站 is famous for its cram schools.
Cram-school teachers are often 名師 with big personalities and catchphrases.
Students say 補數學, 補英文 for taking extra classes in a subject.
opening_line: 來，坐。上次模擬考的成績出來了，我們聊一下好不好？

title: Learning internet slang from a cousin
setting: A café in 西門町 on a Saturday. Your 19-year-old cousin scrolls Dcard, PTT and Threads, reading posts aloud and laughing.
ai_role: 小宇, your sarcastic Gen-Z cousin, fluent in Taiwanese internet slang, who explains memes only after teasing you first.
learner_role: An older cousin who wants to understand what young people are saying online.
goals: Ask what slang terms mean
Use at least three slang terms in context
React to an online post like a Taiwanese netizen (鄉民)

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè yě tài chě le ba!
key_phrases.en: That's ridiculous!
key_phrases.note: 扯 = absurd, unbelievable.

key_phrases.pinyin: shǎ yǎn māo mī.
key_phrases.en: I'm speechless (lit. 'stunned kitty').
key_phrases.note: A playful extension of 傻眼.

key_phrases.pinyin: mǔ tāng o!
key_phrases.en: Don't! / No way!
key_phrases.note: From Taiwanese 毋通 (m̄-thang), 'must not'.

key_phrases.pinyin: tā zhēn de hěn bā qī ê.
key_phrases.en: He's such an idiot.
key_phrases.note: 87 (bā qī) sounds like 白癡 (bái chī); playful, not too harsh.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ zhè ge yuè yào chī tǔ le.
key_phrases.en: I'll be eating dirt this month (I'm broke).

key_phrases.pinyin: bú yào bào léi!
key_phrases.en: No spoilers!
key_phrases.note: 爆雷 = spoil the plot; 雷 alone can mean a bad film or a bad teammate.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè jiù shì xiǎo què xìng a.
key_phrases.en: That's a small but certain happiness.
key_phrases.note: 小確幸 came from a Japanese phrase by Murakami and is hugely popular in Taiwan.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ kě yǐ!
key_phrases.en: I'm totally into that! / I'd go for it!
key_phrases.note: Used about crushes, food or anything appealing.

native_tips: 鄉民 = PTT users (netizens); 推 = upvote, 噓 = downvote.
魯蛇 (loser) and 溫拿 (winner) are English loans.
Slang changes fast; the AI should mark which terms feel dated.
opening_line: 哈哈哈你看這篇，有人在捷運上吃雞排被罵爆，傻眼貓咪欸！

title: A job interview
setting: A tech company's office in 內湖科學園區. Second-round interview in a glass meeting room; a manager has your 履歷 and 自傳 printed out.
ai_role: 陳經理, a professional but friendly hiring manager who asks about strengths, motivation and salary expectations.
learner_role: A candidate interviewing for a project manager position.
goals: Introduce yourself concisely and professionally
Explain your strengths and why you want the job
Ask about the role and state salary expectations

key_phrases.zh: 我在這個領域有三年的工作經驗。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ zài zhè ge lǐng yù yǒu sān nián de gōng zuò jīng yàn.
key_phrases.en: I have three years of experience in this field.

key_phrases.zh: 我的優點是學習能力強，抗壓性也不錯。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ de yōu diǎn shì xué xí néng lì qiáng, kàng yā xìng yě bú cuò.
key_phrases.en: My strengths are that I learn fast and handle pressure well.
key_phrases.note: 抗壓性 (stress tolerance) is a common Taiwan HR term.

key_phrases.zh: 我之所以應徵這個職缺，是因為貴公司重視創新。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ zhī suǒ yǐ yìng zhēng zhè ge zhí quē, shì yīn wèi guì gōng sī zhòng shì chuàng xīn.
key_phrases.en: I applied for this opening because your company values innovation.
key_phrases.note: 職缺 = job opening; 貴公司 = your (esteemed) company.

key_phrases.zh: 請問這個職位的主要工作內容是什麼？
key_phrases.pinyin: qǐng wèn zhè ge zhí wèi de zhǔ yào gōng zuò nèi róng shì shén me?
key_phrases.en: What are the main responsibilities of this position?

key_phrases.zh: 我的期望薪資是月薪六萬左右。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ de qí wàng xīn zī shì yuè xīn liù wàn zuǒ yòu.
key_phrases.en: My expected salary is around 60,000 a month.
key_phrases.note: Taiwan reads 期 as qí.

key_phrases.pinyin: qǐng wèn shì yòng qí duō jiǔ?
key_phrases.en: How long is the probation period?

native_tips: Taiwanese applications often require a 自傳 (short autobiography) along with the 履歷; 104人力銀行 is the main job site.
Use 您 and 貴公司 throughout.
Salary is discussed as monthly pay plus how many months of 年終 (year-end bonus).
opening_line: 您好，請坐。今天謝謝您過來，先請您簡單自我介紹一下好嗎？

title: Meeting your partner's parents
setting: Sunday lunch at your partner's family home in 台中. The table is crowded with dishes, the TV is on mute, and the parents, in their sixties, are clearly a little nervous too.
ai_role: 林媽媽, your partner's mother: warm but curious, asks about your job, family and plans, and keeps putting food in your bowl.
learner_role: Someone meeting a partner's parents for the first time.
goals: Greet the parents properly and present a gift
Answer questions about your work and background
Compliment the food and thank them on leaving

key_phrases.zh: 伯父、伯母好，這是一點小心意。
key_phrases.pinyin: bó fù, bó mǔ hǎo, zhè shì yì diǎn xiǎo xīn yì.
key_phrases.en: Hello, uncle and auntie, this is a small gift.
key_phrases.note: Address a partner's parents as 伯父/伯母 or 叔叔/阿姨. Bring a 伴手禮 such as fruit or 鳳梨酥.

key_phrases.zh: 不用麻煩了，我自己來就好。
key_phrases.pinyin: bú yòng má fán le, wǒ zì jǐ lái jiù hǎo.
key_phrases.en: Please don't trouble yourself, I'll help myself.

key_phrases.zh: 伯母，這道菜好好吃，是怎麼做的？
key_phrases.pinyin: bó mǔ, zhè dào cài hǎo hǎo chī, shì zěn me zuò de?
key_phrases.en: Auntie, this dish is delicious, how do you make it?

key_phrases.zh: 我現在在一家科技公司上班。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xiàn zài zài yì jiā kē jì gōng sī shàng bān.
key_phrases.en: I currently work at a tech company.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ chī hěn bǎo le, xiè xie.
key_phrases.en: I'm very full, thank you.
key_phrases.note: Expect to say this several times.

key_phrases.zh: 謝謝招待，下次換我們請您吃飯。
key_phrases.pinyin: xiè xie zhāo dài, xià cì huàn wǒ men qǐng nín chī fàn.
key_phrases.en: Thank you for having me; next time we'll treat you.

native_tips: Modesty is valued: deflect compliments with 哪裡哪裡 or 還好啦.
Offer to help clear the table or wash dishes even if they refuse.
Questions about salary, family and marriage plans are normal; answer warmly and briefly.
opening_line: 哎呀，你就是小婷常常說的那個朋友喔？快進來坐，路上塞不塞車？

title: Small talk about an election
setting: Lunch with coworkers a week before local elections. Campaign trucks blast slogans outside, candidate posters cover every overpass, and the TV in the restaurant shows political talk shows.
ai_role: 志明, an opinionated but polite coworker. The AI stays balanced and does not endorse any party.
learner_role: A coworker curious about how Taiwanese elections work.
goals: Ask whether people are going home to vote and why
Discuss which issues matter to people
Keep the conversation respectful and neutral

key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ zhè cì huì huí qù tóu piào ma?
key_phrases.en: Are you going home to vote this time?
key_phrases.note: You must vote where your household is registered (戶籍地), so many people travel home.

key_phrases.zh: 我戶籍在高雄，要坐高鐵回去投。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ hù jí zài gāo xióng, yào zuò gāo tiě huí qù tóu.
key_phrases.en: My household registration is in Kaohsiung, so I'll take the HSR back to vote.

key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ bǐ jiào zài yì nǎ xiē zhèng jiàn?
key_phrases.en: Which policy proposals matter most to you?

key_phrases.zh: 宣傳車每天早上都好吵喔。
key_phrases.pinyin: xuān chuán chē měi tiān zǎo shàng dōu hǎo chǎo o.
key_phrases.en: The campaign trucks are so noisy every morning.

key_phrases.zh: 投票是個人的自由，我們互相尊重就好。
key_phrases.pinyin: tóu piào shì gè rén de zì yóu, wǒ men hù xiāng zūn zhòng jiù hǎo.
key_phrases.en: Voting is a personal choice; let's just respect each other.

key_phrases.pinyin: dòng suàn!
key_phrases.en: Get elected! (rally chant)
key_phrases.note: 凍蒜 imitates Taiwanese 當選 (tòng-suán).

native_tips: Party colours: 藍 (KMT), 綠 (DPP), 白 (TPP). People may ask 你是藍的還是綠的？; a vague answer is fine.
Election day has no campaigning, and results come in fast the same evening.
Politics can be sensitive at work and with family; many people avoid the topic.
opening_line: 欸，下禮拜就要投票了，你會回家投嗎？

title: A high-school reunion
setting: A restaurant in 彰化, ten years after graduation. Old class photos play on a screen, the 班導 has been invited, and everyone is guessing who married whom. It feels like the world of 《那些年》.
ai_role: 志豪, your former deskmate: now an engineer, a bit heavier, loves teasing everyone about old crushes and embarrassing stories.
learner_role: A former classmate who hasn't been back in years.
goals: Greet old friends and catch up on their lives
Reminisce about teachers, exams and crushes
Make a toast to your youth

key_phrases.zh: 好久不見！你都沒什麼變耶！
key_phrases.pinyin: hǎo jiǔ bú jiàn! nǐ dōu méi shén me biàn ye!
key_phrases.en: Long time no see! You haven't changed at all!

key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ hái jì de wǒ men bān dǎo ma?
key_phrases.en: Do you remember our homeroom teacher?
key_phrases.note: 班導 (班導師) = homeroom teacher; mainland 班主任.

key_phrases.zh: 那時候大家都暗戀我們班的班花。
key_phrases.pinyin: nà shí hòu dà jiā dōu àn liàn wǒ men bān de bān huā.
key_phrases.en: Back then everyone had a crush on the prettiest girl in our class.
key_phrases.note: Many Taiwanese say 時候 with a full fourth tone: shí hòu.

key_phrases.zh: 早知道當年就跟她告白了。
key_phrases.pinyin: zǎo zhī dào dāng nián jiù gēn tā gào bái le.
key_phrases.en: If I'd known, I would have confessed to her back then.

key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ xiàn zài zài nǎ lǐ gāo jiù?
key_phrases.en: Where are you working these days?
key_phrases.note: 高就 is a polite (often joking) way to ask about someone's job.

key_phrases.pinyin: lái, jìng wǒ men de qīng chūn!
key_phrases.en: Here's to our youth!

native_tips: Reunions are full of teasing; laugh along and tease back.
Expect questions like 結婚了沒？有小孩了嗎？
Mild expletives like 哇靠 are common among old classmates; the novel uses them constantly.
opening_line: 哇靠，真的是你喔！十年沒見了耶，你現在住哪？還記得高三坐你後面的我嗎？

title: A breakup conversation
setting: A quiet café near 師大 on a rainy weeknight. You and your partner of two years sit opposite each other, drinks untouched.
ai_role: 子晴, your partner: calm but sad, wants honest answers and to end things kindly.
learner_role: A partner who also feels the relationship isn't working.
goals: Express your feelings honestly and gently
Explain why the relationship isn't working without blaming
Discuss what happens next and end respectfully

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men hǎo hǎo tán yì tán, hǎo ma?
key_phrases.en: Let's talk this through properly, OK?

key_phrases.zh: 最近我們好像一直在吵架。
key_phrases.pinyin: zuì jìn wǒ men hǎo xiàng yì zhí zài chǎo jià.
key_phrases.en: Lately it feels like we argue all the time.

key_phrases.zh: 不是你的問題，是我們真的不適合。
key_phrases.pinyin: bú shì nǐ de wèn tí, shì wǒ men zhēn de bú shì hé.
key_phrases.en: It's not your fault, we're just not right for each other.

key_phrases.zh: 我需要一點時間冷靜一下。
key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ xū yào yì diǎn shí jiān lěng jìng yí xià.
key_phrases.en: I need some time to calm down.

key_phrases.pinyin: xiè xie nǐ zhè liǎng nián de péi bàn.
key_phrases.en: Thank you for being with me these two years.

key_phrases.pinyin: wǒ men hái néng dāng péng yǒu ma?
key_phrases.en: Can we still be friends?

native_tips: 好聚好散 (part on good terms) is the ideal people aim for.
Taiwanese often avoid blunt statements; softeners like 好像, 可能, 是不是 are common.
Breaking up over LINE is considered cold; doing it face to face is more respectful.
opening_line: 你來了。我想了很久……我們是不是應該好好談一下了？

title: Consoling a friend
setting: Late night on a riverside path in 新店. Your close friend texted 「出來走走？」 an hour ago; he has just been laid off and is pretending to be fine.
ai_role: 小傑, a close friend who just lost his job, jokes to hide how upset he is, and slowly opens up.
learner_role: A supportive friend.
goals: Notice and acknowledge your friend's feelings
Listen and offer comfort without lecturing
Offer concrete help

key_phrases.pinyin: nǐ hái hǎo ma? xiǎng liáo liáo ma?
key_phrases.en: Are you OK? Want to talk?

key_phrases.zh: 這不是你的錯，不要太自責。
key_phrases.pinyin: zhè bú shì nǐ de cuò, bú yào tài zì zé.
key_phrases.en: This isn't your fault, don't blame yourself too much.

key_phrases.pinyin: xiǎng kū jiù kū ba, wǒ péi nǐ.
key_phrases.en: Cry if you want to, I'm here.

key_phrases.zh: 有什麼需要幫忙的，隨時跟我說。
key_phrases.pinyin: yǒu shén me xū yào bāng máng de, suí shí gēn wǒ shuō.
key_phrases.en: If you need anything, tell me anytime.

key_phrases.zh: 先好好休息，工作再找就有。
key_phrases.pinyin: xiān hǎo hǎo xiū xí, gōng zuò zài zhǎo jiù yǒu.
key_phrases.en: Rest properly first; you'll find another job.

key_phrases.pinyin: zǒu, wǒ qǐng nǐ chī xiāo yè.
key_phrases.en: Come on, late-night snack on me.
key_phrases.note: Treating someone to 宵夜 is a classic way of showing care.

native_tips: 加油 is used for encouragement everywhere, but in grief it can sound shallow; 我陪你 is warmer.
Taiwanese friends often show support through food and company rather than long speeches.
資遣 = laid off with severance (a Taiwan legal term).
opening_line: 沒事啦，我很好啊……只是今天被公司資遣了而已。哈。

title: Giving a short presentation at work
setting: Monday 10am weekly meeting (週會) in a conference room. The projector is on, your slides are ready, and three managers are looking at their laptops.
ai_role: 黃副理, your attentive manager, who interrupts with tough follow-up questions about numbers.
learner_role: An employee presenting quarterly results.
goals: Open the presentation formally
Present data and explain causes
Handle a question you cannot answer on the spot

key_phrases.zh: 各位主管、同事早安，今天由我來報告第三季的成果。
key_phrases.pinyin: gè wèi zhǔ guǎn, tóng shì zǎo ān, jīn tiān yóu wǒ lái bào gào dì sān jì de chéng guǒ.
key_phrases.en: Good morning, managers and colleagues. Today I'll report on our Q3 results.

key_phrases.zh: 請大家看一下這張圖表。
key_phrases.pinyin: qǐng dà jiā kàn yí xià zhè zhāng tú biǎo.
key_phrases.en: Please take a look at this chart.

key_phrases.zh: 跟上一季相比，營收成長了百分之十二。
key_phrases.pinyin: gēn shàng yí jì xiāng bǐ, yíng shōu chéng zhǎng le bǎi fēn zhī shí èr.
key_phrases.en: Compared with last quarter, revenue grew 12%.
key_phrases.note: 營收 = revenue.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhǔ yào yuán yīn yǒu sān diǎn: dì yī……
key_phrases.en: There are three main reasons. First…

key_phrases.zh: 這部分我會後再確認，再回覆您。
key_phrases.pinyin: zhè bù fèn wǒ huì hòu zài què rèn, zài huí fù nín.
key_phrases.en: I'll check that after the meeting and get back to you.
key_phrases.note: 回覆 = reply (Taiwan usage).

key_phrases.zh: 以上是我的報告，請問大家有沒有什麼問題？
key_phrases.pinyin: yǐ shàng shì wǒ de bào gào, qǐng wèn dà jiā yǒu méi yǒu shén me wèn tí?
key_phrases.en: That's my report. Are there any questions?

native_tips: 簡報 = slides/presentation; 報告 = to report.
Taiwanese offices mix English terms freely: KPI, deadline, meeting, case.
Promising to 會後確認 is better than guessing an answer.
opening_line: 好，時間差不多了，接下來請你報告這一季的進度。

title: A podcast chat about Taiwanese food culture
setting: A small podcast studio in 台北 with foam on the walls and two microphones. The episode topic is the north-south divide in Taiwanese food.
ai_role: 阿Ben, a witty foodie host from 台南 who fiercely defends southern sweetness and loves provoking guests.
learner_role: A guest who has eaten their way around Taiwan.
goals: Describe your favourite Taiwanese foods vividly
Discuss north-south differences with examples
Give an opinion on what food means in Taiwanese culture

key_phrases.zh: 北部的滷肉飯，在南部通常叫肉燥飯。
key_phrases.pinyin: běi bù de lǔ ròu fàn, zài nán bù tōng cháng jiào ròu zào fàn.
key_phrases.en: What the north calls 滷肉飯 is usually called 肉燥飯 in the south.

key_phrases.zh: 台南的東西真的比較甜嗎？
key_phrases.pinyin: tái nán de dōng xī zhēn de bǐ jiào tián ma?
key_phrases.en: Is food in Tainan really sweeter?

key_phrases.zh: 南部粽是用水煮的，北部粽是用蒸的。
key_phrases.pinyin: nán bù zòng shì yòng shuǐ zhǔ de, běi bù zòng shì yòng zhēng de.
key_phrases.en: Southern zongzi are boiled, northern ones are steamed.

key_phrases.pinyin: zhè jiù shì suǒ wèi de gǔ zǎo wèi.
key_phrases.en: This is what they call 'old-time flavour'.
key_phrases.note: 古早 from Taiwanese kóo-tsá, 'olden days'.

key_phrases.zh: 對我來說，小吃代表的是一種記憶。
key_phrases.pinyin: duì wǒ lái shuō, xiǎo chī dài biǎo de shì yì zhǒng jì yì.
key_phrases.en: For me, street food represents a kind of memory.

key_phrases.zh: 珍珠奶茶到底是誰發明的，到現在還有爭議。
key_phrases.pinyin: zhēn zhū nǎi chá dào dǐ shì shéi fā míng de, dào xiàn zài hái yǒu zhēng yì.
key_phrases.en: Who actually invented bubble tea is still disputed.
key_phrases.note: Taiwan commonly says shéi for 誰.
